summary.name: Helix
summary.one_liner: Helix is a post-modern modal text editor built in Rust for the terminal, with multiple selections, tree-sitter syntax handling, and built-in language server support.
use_cases: code navigation by functions and classes
using an IDE-like editor without extra configuration
switching from Vim or Kakoune with fewer config files
summary.what_it_does: Helix is a terminal-based modal text editor written in Rust, with no Electron, VimScript, or JavaScript dependencies, so it can be used over ssh, in tmux, or in a plain terminal. It uses multiple selections as a core editing primitive, inspired by Kakoune, so commands act on all selections at once. Tree-sitter provides syntax highlighting, indent calculation, and navigation/selection of syntax nodes such as functions, classes, and comments. Language server support gives auto completion, goto definition, documentation, and diagnostics without additional configuration. Built-in extras include a fuzzy finder for files and symbols, project-wide search, themes, auto-closing bracket pairs, and surround integration.
notable: Multiple selections and cursors inspired by Kakoune
Tree-sitter based highlighting and syntax-node selection
Built-in language server support with no extra configuration
caveats: No plugin system is currently available; the project intends to add one eventually
No GUI frontend yet; a WebGPU-based frontend is only being prototyped
